tagline: Up SC 107 through the forest to the Jocassee overlook.
intro: SC 107 climbs north into the Blue Ridge through the Sumter National Forest, two winding lanes with forest on both sides, turnouts for the mountain views and picnic waysides along the way. Just north of the Cherry Hill campground Moody Spring runs on the east side of the road, cool mountain water for anyone with a bottle.

Just before the state line, Burrell's Place Pull-off remembers a B-25 that crashed into a mountaintop one night in March 1943. The wreck was found eleven days later, when a boy's horse shied at one of its engines on the Moody Trail.
season: Discover South Carolina calls the road especially fine in the fall color season and in early summer, when the rhododendron bloom.

moments.title: Oconee State Park
moments.text: Near the foot of the road the Civilian Conservation Corps built this park in the 1930s, and the Foothills Trail has its southern end here.

moments.title: Kings Creek Falls
moments.text: A spur road off the byway leads to the trailheads, an easy twenty minutes to Spoonauger Falls and a harder mile on to the falls on Kings Creek, bound for the Chattooga.

moments.title: Wigington Overlook
moments.text: Off SC 413 the view runs out over Lake Jocassee, which in 1973 drowned a churchyard where a scene from Deliverance had been filmed, now 130 feet down.

sources.label: Discover South Carolina, Take a scenic drive along one of South Carolina's prettiest mountain roads
